preconditions.expression: all(c in '()?' for c in stdin.splitlines()[0])
preconditions.description: Every character in each test case line is either '(', ')', or '?'
The first line is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000), and there are exactly t test cases following it

preconditions.expression: all(2 <= len(s) <= 100 for s in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case string s has length between 2 and 100 (inclusive)

preconditions.expression: all(s.count('(') == 1 and s.count(')') == 1 for s in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each test case string s contains exactly one '(' and exactly one ')'

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line in ['YES', 'NO', 'yes', 'no', 'Yes', 'No'] for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output line is a case-insensitive YES/NO indicating whether the corresponding test case can be replaced to form an RBS

postconditions.expression: all((stdout_line == 'YES' or stdout_line == 'YES'.lower()) if any(all(c == '(' or c == ')' for c in s) and is_rbs(s) for s in possible_replacements(s)) else (stdout_line == 'NO' or stdout_line == 'NO'.lower()) for s, stdout_line in zip(stdin.splitlines()[1:], stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: For each test case s, the output is YES if and only if there exists at least one way to replace all '?' in s with '(' or ')' such that the resulting string is a regular bracket sequence (RBS). An RBS is defined as a sequence that can be transformed into a correct arithmetic expression by inserting '+' and '1' (i.e., balanced parentheses with exactly one '(' and one ')' after replacement)
